extracted.intended_audience: Researchers applying to DFG funding programmes and DFG reviewers/administrative staff
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and quality-assurance criteria for reviewing and deciding on research funding proposals submitted to the German Research Foundation (DFG). Covers reviewer guidance, programme-specific notes, procedural checks, and the DFG's QA process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniform review standards / General Guidelines for Reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: The DFG provides all reviewers with appropriate guidance so as to ensure that proposals under all the various DFG programmes are reviewed according to the same standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers are given the 'General Guidelines for Reviews' (linked) to ensure consistent application of standards across DFG programmes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Programme-specific additional review notes
rubrics_metrics.description: To take account of the specific details of the various programmes, additional review notes are provided for individual programmes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers and applicants should consult the programme-specific review notes (available via the full list with filter 'review') for criteria or emphases that differ by funding programme.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality assurance: content and formal accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: The DFG pursues quality assurance in its procedures in relation to both the quality of content and formal accuracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: QA covers both substantive research quality and compliance with formal/procedural rules; both dimensions are subject to checks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three-stage assessment of research quality
rubrics_metrics.description: As a rule, the research quality of a project is assessed by means of a three-stage process: first by reviewers, then by the review boards and finally by the Joint Committee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funding decisions reflect a sequential evaluation: external/internal reviewers -> review boards -> Joint Committee. See linked page 'How does the DFG decide whether a proposal is to receive funding?' for process details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal quality assurance performed by Head Office unit (Quality and Programme Management)
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition to the subject-based review process, the DFG operates a formal quality assurance system at its Head Office. This involves each proposal being checked to ensure applicants have complied with the procedural rules of the respective funding programme.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Quality and Programme Management unit is independent of the departments that process proposals and is responsible for formal QA before final decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural checks required before final decision
rubrics_metrics.description: Before the final decision on a proposal is arrived at the following points are checked, for example: Is the applicant entitled to submit the proposal? Are the decision documents consistent and has the necessary number of reviews been carried out? Do the reviews possibly contain discriminatory statements? Has a statement by an ethics committee been submitted in cases where studies are to be carried out on humans, on material taken from humans or using identifiable personal data?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These explicit checks are applied to ensure procedural correctness: applicant eligibility, consistency of decision documents, sufficiency of reviews, absence of discriminatory language in reviews, and required ethics approvals for human-related research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aim of QA: identify/correct procedural errors and ensure equal treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: The aim of this quality assurance is to identify and correct any procedural errors and to raise awareness at the Head Office to sources of error, thereby ensuring equal treatment of all proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: QA both remedies errors and informs institutional improvements so that all proposals are treated equally and fairly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject Area Structure and Interdisciplinarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Header indicating consideration of subject area structure and interdisciplinarity in the review framework.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page lists this as a dimension (no further detail provided on this page); implies reviewers should consider subject-area structure and interdisciplinary aspects where relevant.
